summary: Thurston County, WA lookout towers from 1929 to 1967 or 1968 (sources differ); the summit now shows tower footings and communication towers.

facts.design: Successive towers: 1929 tripod on four topped trees with an 84 ft floor; 1935 100 ft timber ring tower with 8x8 cab; 1954 45 ft tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Final tower removed in 1967 or 1968 (sources differ); a 2020 photo caption and a 1975 survey describe communication towers and footings on the summit, not a lookout

access.note: Willhite's 2020 photo note: a gate with a large parking area, and visitors walk the road to the summit view. No legal access rules are stated; verify before editing.

visit.trail_note: Short road walk from the gate to the summit, per Willhite

events.note: Tripod tower on four topped trees with an 84 ft floor; 114 ft per register, 119 ft to the lookout floor per Timberman account (a 1929 report on the Forest Lookouts page gives 119 ft total)
Register and firelookout.com say blew down; Willhite says an annual report suggests it was brought down
100 ft creosoted timber ring tower with 8x8 cab
Removed by the U.S. Army to make room for a radar station (firelookout.com says destroyed)
Register says one source reports an 83 ft tower with 7x7 cab built in 1943
83 ft tower blew down (register); Forest Lookouts quotes a 1946 report saying it was demolished by wind
Register says a 68 ft wooden tower replaced it; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1946 report of an 83 ft ring tower built to replace it
45 ft wooden tower with L-4 cab
Removed in the DNR's first round of phasing out lookouts; Willhite's photo captions say 1968
Survey team noted several microwave and communication towers scattered around the summit
Registered November 27, 2011 as US 1160, WA 68; nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.proposed: remove, or record height per tower
corrections.why: 30.5 m (100 ft) is the height of the 1935 tower only. The sources give the 1929 tower 114 to 119 ft and later towers 45 to 83 ft, so one height for the site misleads.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 114 ft; a 1930 Timberman account quoted by Forest Lookouts and Willhite gives 119 ft from ground to lookout floor, and a 1929 report on the Forest Lookouts page gives 119 ft total. Not resolved; both figures are reported in the story.
Register and firelookout.com say the tower blew down in 1934; Willhite says an annual report suggests it was brought down. Cause not resolved.
Register and firelookout.com say 1967; Willhite's photo captions say 1968, and a 1968 survey made no mention of lookout towers. Not resolved.
Register says a 68 ft wooden tower replaced the wind-felled tower that year; Forest Lookouts quotes a 1946 report of an 83 ft ring tower built to replace one demolished by wind. Not resolved.
firelookout.com gives 12 miles SW of Olympia (the story uses this, with 'about'); a 1929 report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page says some 18 miles west of Olympia. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Proposed correction: the brief's height_m of 30.5 matches only the 1935 tower. Dates for the 1943 to 1946 towers and the 1967 vs 1968 removal are contested across sources. Access level 'public' rests on a 2020 photo note of visitors walking up from a gate, which Willhite qualifies with 'while it lasts'; no source states legal access rules, so verify the gate status before editing. No lookout staff are named in the sources read; people in photo captions (1952, 1953) are not described as lookouts and are not used. No web search was possible for this run (budget used up).
